methodological_rigor.justification: Retrospective study of thyroid cancer reoperation (N=375 total, N=101 US-only vs N=62 US+MRI after propensity matching). Compares diagnostic performance (sensitivity/specificity for central lymph node metastasis), surgical metrics, and oncologic outcomes. Propensity matching strengthens comparability. Cox regression for recurrence-free survival analysis. However, retrospective design, single-center origin, propensity matching limitations, and relatively small matched groups (101 vs 62) limit rigor.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Addresses important clinical question of imaging modalities for preoperative assessment in thyroid cancer reoperation. Demonstrates US+MRI improves diagnostic sensitivity (52.5% to 90.9%) and affects surgical approach (higher CND rates, greater lymph node yield). Improves biochemical response rates. Directly relevant to surgical planning. LoE limited by retrospective design but clinically meaningful.

reporting_quality.justification: Describes study populations, propensity matching process, diagnostic criteria (central node detection, biochemical response), and surgical outcomes. Kaplan-Meier curves for RFS presented. However, no explicit STROBE adherence statement. Data and code availability not mentioned. Methods section could be more detailed regarding imaging protocols.

novelty_literature.justification: Combined imaging assessment for thyroid cancer well-established. Study confirms expected benefit of MRI addition to US. Limited novelty; primarily validation of imaging strategy in single-center cohort. Incremental contribution documenting improved diagnostic performance.

writing_presentation.justification: Well-organized manuscript with clear presentation of imaging comparison. Methods section describes both imaging modalities and surgical assessment protocols. Results effectively communicate diagnostic performance improvements and surgical outcomes. Discussion appropriately contextualizes findings within guidelines (2025 ATA, NCCN). Publication-ready quality.

key_strengths: Demonstrates US+MRI significantly improves diagnostic sensitivity for central lymph node metastasis (52.5% → 90.9%) in thyroid cancer reoperation
Propensity matching strengthens comparability of imaging groups despite retrospective design
Higher rates of central neck dissection and greater lymph node yield in combined imaging group
Improved biochemical response rates (50.0% vs 27.7%) with combined approach
Comparable complication rates suggest safety of improved diagnostic imaging strategy
key_concerns: Retrospective single-center design limits generalizability; different results possible at other institutions
Propensity-matched groups still relatively small (101 vs 62); adequate statistical power uncertain
Overall recurrence-free survival not significantly different between groups; benefit mainly in high-risk subset
No explicit statement regarding data availability or reproducibility
Selection bias possible; reasons for choosing US+MRI or US-only not detailed
MRI cost-effectiveness not addressed despite increased resource utilization
chief_reviewer.rationale: Competent retrospective study demonstrating diagnostic value of combining MRI with US in thyroid cancer reoperation planning. Suitable for Tier 3 journals (Thyroid, Cancer Medicine, European Journal of Surgical Oncology) as practical imaging guidance with improved surgical outcomes in select high-risk patients.
